\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{خسیس} (khasis)}{خسیس (khasis)}]{\fa{خسیس} (khasis) — stingy}

\label{lesson:FA-C236-khasis}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for free of charge, then the Persian for unemployed.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{خسیس}}
\textbf{\fa{خسیس}} — \emph{khasis} — \textquotedblleft{}stingy\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{khasis} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{ḫasīs}, \textquotedblleft{}mean, base\textquotedblright{}. Its Arabic root is \emph{ḫ-s-s} (Lane).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{بامزه} (bâmaze)}{بامزه (bâmaze)}]{\fa{بامزه} (bâmaze) — funny, cute}

\label{lesson:FA-C236-bamaze}

Before the new one: say the Persian for unemployed, then the Persian for stingy.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{بامزه}}
\textbf{\fa{بامزه}} — \emph{bâmaze} — \textquotedblleft{}funny, cute\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bâmaze} is built from \emph{bâ}, \textquotedblleft{}with\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{maze}, \textquotedblleft{}taste, flavour\textquotedblright{}: with flavour, so lively and funny. Both are native Persian words, inherited rather than borrowed.
\end{cousinweb}

\label{lesson:FA-C236-divane}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for funny, then the Persian for interesting.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{دیوانه}}
\textbf{\fa{دیوانه}} — \emph{divâne} — \textquotedblleft{}crazy\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{divâne} is usually explained as built from \emph{div}, \textquotedblleft{}demon\textquotedblright{} (Middle Persian \emph{dēw}), and the ending \emph{-âne}: possessed by a demon. Both pieces are inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{وفادار} (vafâdâr)}{وفادار (vafâdâr)}]{\fa{وفادار} (vafâdâr) — loyal}

\label{lesson:FA-C236-vafadar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for interesting, then the Persian for crazy.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{وفادار}}
\textbf{\fa{وفادار}} — \emph{vafâdâr} — \textquotedblleft{}loyal\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{vafâdâr} is \emph{vafâ}, \textquotedblleft{}loyalty\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{-dâr}, \textquotedblleft{}holding\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB). \emph{vafâ} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{wafāʾ}, \textquotedblleft{}keeping faith\textquotedblright{} (root \emph{w-f-y}, Lane); \emph{-dâr} is native Persian.
\end{cousinweb}
